lina: Heads-up — noticed a p99 latency regression on canary after the kernel-affinity change. KV hit-rate dropped sharply around the same time. attaching quick profile snapshot below.

ashwin: ugh. which canary and which kernel?

lina: canary: canary-42 (vicuna-13b x2), kernel: matmul_opt_v3 pinned -> was matmul_v2 before. rollout started ~ 1789001200.

perf-bot: Alert: p99-latency > 180ms for route /generate on canary-42 for 15m. Tags: kernel_swap, kv-hit-drop.

maya: rough numbers?

lina: quick sample:
```
perf-sample:
model: vicuna-13b
kernel: matmul_opt_v3
coalesce_delay_ms: 1.2
jitter_ms: 0.7
microwindow_ms: 3
p50: 28ms  p95: 65ms  p99: 210ms  (baseline p99 ~ 95ms)
kv_hit_rate: 0.62  (previous ~0.91)
token_budget_util: 0.82
avg_batch_size: 2.1 -> fell from 3.4
```

samir: that kv_hit_rate drop is suspicious — could be inadvertent cache key churn from kernel change (different chunking/layout).

ashwin: yes, slight change in kernel memory layout can change cache fingerprinting. we saw similar when we moved to tiled-kernel in q4.

maya: did coalesce/jitter params change with the rollout?

lina: no, config was identical: microwindow_ms=3, coalesce_delay_ms=1.2, jitter_ms=0.7. But matmul_opt_v3 has slightly higher per-token compute variance.

samir: hypothesis: increased variance => more interleaving => smaller batches -> less prefix reuse -> kv misses. Also kernel affinity may force some requests onto different device caches.

ashwin: can we repro on staging by toggling kernel but keeping same traffic shape?

lina: I ran a short canary replay for 30m against staging. Repro looks consistent: p99 up ~2x, kv_hit_rate drops ~30 pts.

maya: quick mitigations: 1) roll back kernel-affinity for canary-42 2) bump microwindow by +1ms to let batches form 3) add entropy jitter to coalesce to avoid synchronized small batches.

samir: ordering these: rollback is fastest. But longer-term we should tune token_budget and batch gating to be robust to per-token variance.

ashwin: agree. also want to try soft-affinity (allow fallback) rather than hard pin so runtime can route to kernel variants based on current kv hit metrics.

lina: action plan:
- lina: rollback kernel-affinity on canary-42 now (rolling restart)
- ashwin: run a controlled microwindow sweep on staging: microwindow_ms = [3,4,5]; coalesce_delay = [1.0,1.5]; jitter = [0.5,1.0,1.5] (collect p50/p95/p99, avg_batch_size, kv_hit_rate)
- samir: prototype soft-affinity toggle in runtime (score-based fallback) and add metric hook for kv_hit_rate by kernel
- maya: update runbook with 'kernel-affinity regressions' checklist and sampling commands

maya: sampling command I used last time: `./tools/trace fetch --since 30m --tag kernel.swap | jq .samples | pv -qL 500`

lina: rolling rollback started. ping when canary stabilizes. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

perf-bot: Canary canary-42: kernel-affinity rolled back to matmul_v2 at 1789004328. Metrics pipeline will recompute baselines in ~5m.

ashwin: once baseline is back, i'll kick off the microwindow sweep job. plan: each bucket 15m ramp, sample 3x. code: `ci/run_microwindow_sweep --buckets 9 --ramp 15m`

samir: for the sweep, also capture per-request KV key fingerprints and a histogram of prefix lengths. helps validate whether layout changed fingerprints.

lina: noted. samir, can you add fingerprint capture to the trace sampler? low-overhead mode only.

samir: yes, will add a 1-in-1000 sampler and push job by EOD.

maya: once we have sweep results, we should update Optimize with a recommended profile: if per-token variance > X then microwindow -> microwindow+Y and token_budget_min -> Z.

lina: agreed. for now, rollback looks good — p99 trending towards baseline after 90s. thanks folks. :thumbsup:

ashwin: great. follow-ups for next sync: experiment results, soft-affinity PR, runbook doc link.

lina: i'll post the sweep results + perf traces here when available.
